prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a mortgage application waiting on payslips. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When an application is waiting on payslips, the quickest cases are the ones where the income dates line up cleanly with the application and the latest payslip is clearly within the expected cycle."},{"type":"fact","content":"When payslips are delayed, it helps to set a short, explicit follow-up date and tell the applicant exactly which document is still needed, rather than leaving the case open-ended."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a payslip arrives but the figures differ from the salary stated on the form, I check whether the applicant has had overtime, commission or a recent pay rise before treating it as an issue."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I am waiting on payslips, I prefer to request the most recent three where possible, because patterns in deductions and variable pay are easier to understand than from a single slip."},{"type":"observation","content":"When an employer pays weekly or fortnightly, applicants often need a little more guidance, because the underwriting team may have to look at average earnings over a longer period rather than a simple monthly figure."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a payslip shows statutory or salary sacrifice deductions, I compare the net and gross carefully so I do not mistake a normal deduction for a problem with affordability."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the applicant is close to completion, a missing payslip can still be resolved quickly if I ask for a clear scan or photo rather than waiting for a perfect copy in the post."},{"type":"preference","content":"When payslips are outstanding, I favour a single reminder that combines the missing item, the deadline and the reason it matters, because that tends to get a faster response."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the income comes from multiple jobs, I make sure each set of payslips is labelled properly, otherwise it is easy to overstate affordability or miss an employment gap."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the latest payslip is older than expected, I treat it as a possible sign of a change in employment and pause the case until the applicant confirms whether the job, hours or pay have changed."}]}
